steps.note: Deploy the app so guest orders store '' instead of NULL (valid both before and after the migration). Waits for the rolling update.
Let terminated old pods finish their in-flight requests (they drain for ~3 s) so no more NULL emails are written.
Backfill ids 1..1,000,000: NULL email -> ''. 100k ids per statement, each its own short transaction; only row locks, which the app (insert/select only) never waits on.

steps.note: Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: catalog-only, no table scan, but needs a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. Waits at most 300 ms per try (app queries queued behind it stay well under their 2 s timeout, even the ~1 s /customer read) and retries until there is a gap. From here on no NULL email can be inserted.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE attempt int; BEGIN FOR attempt IN 1..300 LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'orders'::regclass AND conname = 'orders_email_not_null') THEN ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; END IF; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2 + random() * 0.8); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to add the check constraint'; END $$;

steps.note: Safety net: set '' on any NULL email still left (e.g. written by an old pod during the rollout). Normally 0 rows; a sequential scan holding only row locks.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; UPDATE orders SET email = '' WHERE email IS NULL;

steps.note: Validate the check constraint: full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block the app's reads or inserts.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; SET lock_timeout = 0; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL: skips the full-table scan because the validated check constraint already proves there are no NULLs; then drop the now-redundant check. Same short-lock-with-retry pattern.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE attempt int; BEGIN FOR attempt IN 1..300 LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS orders_email_not_null; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2 + random() * 0.8); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to set NOT NULL'; END $$;

steps.note: Check: orders.email is NOT NULL (fails the plan otherwise).
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT (SELECT attnotnull FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'orders'::regclass AND attname = 'email') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.email is still nullable'; END IF; END $$;
